name: shuffle-hero
title: Shuffle Hero
description: A split hero: a small orange eyebrow, a large headline, a short paragraph and a call-to-action button on the left, with a 4x4 grid of photos on the right that springs into a new random order every three seconds.
use: A landing hero sells a visual product and a static image feels too quiet, but the headline still needs to lead.
avoid: The photos reshuffle forever and load from remote URLs, so it costs bandwidth, distracts from reading, and never rests.
a11y: The button is a real button, but the sixteen photos are unlabelled CSS backgrounds and the reshuffle ignores reduced-motion settings. (keyboard: yes, labels: partial, reduced motion: not handled)
looks: On black, a left column carries an orange uppercase eyebrow, a large white two-line headline, a grey paragraph and an orange button. To its right a 4x4 grid of closely spaced square photos shows sports and studio activities, filling roughly half the width.
behaves: Every three seconds the sixteen photos swap places; each tile glides to its new cell with a spring, so briefly the grid opens gaps and tiles overlap before settling. The copy stays put.
customise: There are no props: the eyebrow, headline, paragraph, button text and the sixteen photo URLs are written inside, so all of them need source edits.
weight: moderate: Sixteen remote photos with spring layout animations every three seconds.
demo: Fitness copy: 'Let's change it up a bit', a line about sunrise yoga and late-night spin, and 16 sports photos.
issues: The grid reshuffles every three seconds with no pause, which can distract from reading the copy.
polishWhy: A clean split layout and lively grid; the looping shuffle never pauses and the photos are generic.
